title: Best Sam's Club Dehumidifier (2026): Amana, Keystone & More
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers at Sam's Club
dek: Sam's Club keeps a short dehumidifier list. One standout is easy to recommend, one is solid, and one deserves a hard look before you spend four figures.
description: The best dehumidifier at Sam's Club: the Amana 50-pint with pump, the Keystone 35-pint and MaxxAir commercial units, plus what to check before you buy.
intro: If you're looking for a **dehumidifier at Sam's Club**, the choice is refreshingly short. The club's own dehumidifier page lists three brands: **Amana**, with a 50-pint unit that has a built-in pump; **Keystone**, with a 35-pint model; and **MaxxAir**, with two commercial-grade machines priced well into four figures.

Some buying guides also name Frigidaire and Whynter as Sam's Club brands, but we couldn't find either live on the club's site — and Whynter's own site lists its standalone dehumidifiers as discontinued. Below, we break down the three that are actually there, which one to buy for your space, and why the club price isn't always the best price on the same model.
topPicksLead: The **Amana 50-Pint with Pump (AMND501PAW)** is the best dehumidifier at Sam's Club: full basement capacity and a pump that drains it for you.

products.name: Amana 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Built-In Pump (AMND501PAW)
pros: Built-in pump drains up to a sink or window
50 pints a day for spaces up to about 4,500 sq ft
cons: Larger unit for a single small room
products.whyWeLoveIt: It's the most useful dehumidifier on Sam's Club's list for the place most people need one: a basement without a convenient floor drain. The pump means you can set a target and forget about the bucket.
products.performance: Amana rates it at 50 pints a day for up to roughly 4,500 square feet, with three fan speeds and a pump for continuous drainage. It's the pump-equipped sibling of the AMND501AW and is slightly heavier to house the pump. Amana's name appears in a 2021 CPSC recall of units made by New Widetech, but the recalled models used different, older model-number prefixes than this one. More on the brand in our [Amana guide](/best/best-amana-dehumidifier/).
products.notes: Compare the club price with home-improvement retailers before buying; the same model number has often been listed for less elsewhere.

products.name: Keystone 35-Pint Dehumidifier with Electronic Controls
pros: 35 pints a day for up to about 3,000 sq ft
Built by Midea, a major manufacturer
cons: Club pricing history is hard to pin down
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a family room, large bedroom or mildly damp basement with a floor drain, a 35-pint unit is plenty, and this Keystone keeps things straightforward.
products.performance: Keystone rates it at 35 pints a day for up to about 3,000 square feet. It drains into its bucket or through a gravity hose, which works well if there's a floor drain nearby. Keystone units are built by Midea; Midea's large 2016 recall covered older units made between 2003 and 2013, not the current Keystone lineup. See our [Keystone guide](/best/best-keystone-dehumidifier/) for sibling models.

products.name: MaxxAir Commercial Dehumidifier
pros: Aimed at large spaces and cleanup jobs
cons: No independent spec sheet or capacity rating we could find
Costs several times more than the residential picks
products.whyWeLoveIt: We include it because it's on the shelf, not because we can wholeheartedly recommend it. If you're drying a flooded space or a very large crawl space, a commercial unit makes sense — but you should see real numbers first.
products.performance: MaxxAir, a Ventamatic brand, is best known for RV roof vents and exhaust fans rather than dehumidifiers. We couldn't verify a pints-per-day rating, coverage figure or manufacturer spec sheet for either model beyond Sam's Club's own listing. Ask for the spec sheet before buying, and compare against established options in our [commercial dehumidifier guide](/best/best-commercial-dehumidifier/).

sections.heading: How we pick Sam's Club dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't test dehumidifiers in a lab. We checked which models are actually live on Sam's Club's dehumidifier page, then compared each model number against manufacturer specs, listings at other major retailers and the CPSC recall database.
We ranked on capacity, drainage and the strength of the supporting data, and we note where the identical model is commonly sold for less elsewhere.

items.label: Capacity for your space
items.text: 35 pints for a large room or mildly damp basement; 50 pints for a damp one. See our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/).

items.text: No floor drain near the unit? Choose the pump model. Compare others in our [pump guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/).

blocks.text: For most members, the decision really comes down to one question: is there a floor drain within hose reach of where the unit will sit? If not, the Amana's pump is worth having. If there is, the Keystone does the job in a mid-size space and the Amana handles a bigger, damper one.

Wondering whether to pay more for a premium 50-pint pump unit instead? Our [Amana vs. Friedrich comparison](/compare/amana-vs-friedrich-dehumidifier/) weighs the Amana against a pricier rival with a longer compressor warranty.

sections.heading: The brands that don't check out

blocks.text: Frigidaire and Whynter often appear in lists of Sam's Club dehumidifier brands. We couldn't find a live Sam's Club listing for either. Frigidaire's current dehumidifiers sell widely through other retailers, so you won't miss out. Whynter's own site shows its standalone dehumidifier models as discontinued, with no replacement line announced; see our [Whynter guide](/best/best-whynter-dehumidifier/) for details.

items: **Keystone:** included in Midea's 2016 CPSC recall of about 3.4 million dehumidifiers built from 2003 to 2013 and sold under dozens of brand names. That recall doesn't cover the current Keystone lineup.
**Amana:** named in the 2021 CPSC recall of New Widetech-built dehumidifiers. The recalled units used older model-number prefixes that don't match the current AMND501PAW.
**MaxxAir:** we found no CPSC dehumidifier recall on record.

blocks.text: If you're buying a used or open-box unit of any brand, check the model number and manufacture date at CPSC.gov first.

The **Amana AMND501PAW** is the best dehumidifier at Sam's Club for a basement, thanks to its 50-pint capacity and built-in pump — just compare its price at other retailers first. The **Keystone 35-Pint** is a sensible choice for a large room or a basement with a floor drain. Reserve the **MaxxAir** units for genuine restoration or very large spaces, and only after seeing a real spec sheet. For more options, see our [Costco guide](/best/best-costco-dehumidifier/).

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier at Sam's Club?
faqs.a: The Amana 50-Pint with Pump (AMND501PAW). It covers up to about 4,500 square feet, has three fan speeds and drains continuously through its built-in pump.

faqs.q: What dehumidifier brands does Sam's Club sell?
faqs.a: Its own dehumidifier page currently lists Amana, Keystone and MaxxAir. We couldn't confirm Frigidaire or Whynter as live Sam's Club dehumidifier brands.

faqs.q: Does Sam's Club sell a dehumidifier with a pump?
faqs.a: Yes. The Amana AMND501PAW is a 50-pint dehumidifier with a built-in condensate pump, which lets you drain water up to a sink or out a window instead of emptying a bucket. The Keystone 35-pint model does not have a pump.

faqs.q: Is MaxxAir a good dehumidifier brand?
faqs.a: It's a real brand best known for RV vents and fans. We couldn't find an independent spec sheet or capacity rating for its commercial dehumidifiers, so ask for one before paying commercial prices.

faqs.q: Is the Sam's Club price on the Amana dehumidifier a good deal?
faqs.a: Not always. The same Amana AMND501PAW has often been listed for less at home-improvement retailers, so compare before you buy.

faqs.q: Have any Sam's Club dehumidifiers been recalled?
faqs.a: Keystone and Amana both appear in older CPSC recalls, but those recalls cover earlier models, not the current units Sam's Club sells. We found no MaxxAir dehumidifier recall.
